name: Complete sign-in
description: Runs on the callback leg only, for whichever provider `{provider}` named. The channel's oauth2_login block owns everything that is the same for every provider -- the 302, the signed state cookie and its CSRF binding, PKCE, the code exchange, and for an OIDC provider the id_token check -- fetches the userinfo for a provider that has no id_token (GitHub), and hands this workflow a NORMALISED identity at `metadata.identity` (`provider`, `subject`, `login`, `name`, `picture`): §I made one workflow serve them all by keying on (provider, subject) rather than a GitHub id. Orion retires the spent state cookie itself, so this response sets one cookie, not two. THE SESSION IS SERVER-SIDE: `sid` names a row in `sessions`, written BEFORE the token is signed so a token can never name a row that does not exist, and its expires_at must stay in step with jwt_sign's expires_in. THE ACCOUNT IS UPSERT ON THE IDENTITY: a new (provider, subject) mints a fresh account (soma-pub-auth-upsert), its handle seeded ONCE from the login and its display_name from the provider's name; a returning one only refreshes its cached login, so a competitor who renamed themselves at the provider keeps their handle and their PATCH /v1/me display_name. The deployment-admin promotion is its own write (soma-pub-auth-promote) because two writes to `users` in one statement would race. A SIGN-IN WHILE ANOTHER SESSION IS LIVE IS AN `account` NOTIFICATION, after the session row and allowed to fail without failing the sign-in. WHERE IT SENDS YOU AFTERWARDS: `metadata.oauth.return_to` when the authorize leg carried a vetted `?next=`, otherwise `app_url` -- Orion checks it against `return_to.allow_list` on the way in and seals it into the state, so an unlisted or tampered value simply is not here.

with.name: No identity came back
with.description: Orion stamps `metadata.identity` from a verified id_token or a userinfo fetch; a provider that is neither OIDC nor has a userinfo_url, or a userinfo answer with no subject, leaves it absent. With no subject there is nothing to key the upsert on, so this answers the redirect the callback page knows how to draw, with its own error word, before any write runs. An UNREACHABLE provider is Orion's own 503 and never reaches here. It goes to the callback page and not to return_to: the person is not signed in.

tasks.name: Upsert the account behind the identity
Pin the invites waiting for this login
tasks.description: Every live participant row of this provider and login that no account holds yet is pinned to the one signing in (S3). continue_on_error: an invite left unpinned still admits by login, and sign-in must not fail on it.

tasks.name: Promote a deployment admin
tasks.description: Own statement, not folded into the upsert: both write `users`, and two writes to one table in one statement race. Reads the same identity the upsert did, so a fresh admin account is created a competitor and promoted here in the same sign-in. Only ever promotes; PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id} is every other change.

input.query: SELECT u.id, u.handle FROM identities i JOIN users u ON u.id = i.user_id WHERE i.provider = ($1)::text AND i.subject = ($2)::text
INSERT INTO sessions (sid, user_id, expires_at, user_agent) VALUES (($1)::uuid, ($2)::uuid, now() + interval '30 days', ($3)::text)

tasks.name: Tell the account's other sessions about this one
tasks.description: Only when another session was already live: a first sign-in, or one after every other session ended, is not news to anyone. After record_session, so the new row exists and is excluded by sid rather than by time. continue_on_error, because a notification must never be the reason a sign-in fails -- the cookie below is the whole point of this workflow. Keyed on the new sid, which is minted once per sign-in, so a retried request cannot say it twice.
